subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, streaming & concurrency
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holloway <sara.holloway@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, streaming & concurrency

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + a few clarifying items so our infra/solutions team can lock in numbers: 

Recap (short):
- Primary use case: batch + interactive clinical summarization for notes ingestion, occasional long-form Q/A.
- Desired latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms for interactive UX, bulk ingestion can tolerate higher latency (<= 2s).
- Current plan: start with hosted endpoint, evaluate Dedicated if throughput grows.

Clarifying items we need from you (helps pin config):
1) Typical and peak concurrent active sessions hitting the inference endpoint? (requests/sec and concurrent open streams)
2) Typical input size distribution (tokens): mean, 95th, and max examples for both "document ingest" and "interactive" flows.
3) Do you need streaming responses for interactive sessions (partial tokens as they’re generated) or is end-of-response acceptable?
4) Any hard max input+output token limits (e.g., we must not truncate above X tokens)?

I attached the SLO worksheet we mentioned — fill whatever you have and we’ll use it to propose a config. Next steps: if you can drop the worksheet back by EOD Thursday our solutions eng will produce expected latency curves (p95) for three model+quantization points and a recommended concurrency cap.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acuity_slo_req.xlsx (SLO spreadsheet stub)
From: Sara Holloway <sara.holloway@acuityhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 17:10:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, streaming & concurrency

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached a small sample latency export we pulled from our staging gateway.

Answers:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~120 concurrent interactive users during clinic hours; burst to ~300 for batched uploads at 02:00 daily. Sustained interactive TPS ~40, bursts to 150.
- Input size (tokens) — interactive: mean 320, p95 1,100, max seen 4,200 (rare). Document ingest: mean 4,500, p95 12,000, max 25,000 (we currently chunk before sending).
- Streaming: yes, interactive UX requires streaming token-by-token for the clinician UI (partial updates are important). Batched ingest does not need streaming.
- Hard token limits: We cannot truncate clinical notes above 30k tokens without manual review; prefer the platform support up to 32k input + 4k output for some critical pipelines.

Attachments: latency_samples_stage.csv

I’ll try to fill out the workbook tonight but wanted to get numbers to you quickly.

—Sara
Sara Holloway
Head of AI Platform, AcuityHealth
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holloway <sara.holloway@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 18:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, streaming & concurrency

Sara — perfect, that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups so our latency projections are accurate: 

1) For the interactive p95 sizes you gave (1,100 tokens p95, max 4,200), are those measured as input-only or input+expected assistant output? If input-only, what is the typical assistant response size we should assume for p95 and max scenarios?

2) For your request to support up to 32k input + 4k output, can you flag which percent of traffic falls into that "very long" bucket (e.g., <1%, 1-5%, 5-10%)? We model long-context perf differently and it materially changes expected p95 latency.

3) Streaming behavior: do you need guaranteed first-byte within X ms after request start (e.g., first chunk within 150ms)? If you have a target for time-to-first-token that will help our runtime tuning (kernel selection, prefill limits).

Suggested next steps:
- If you can add the assistant response token estimates in the workbook, we’ll run 3 profiles (short: <=1k, mid: 1k–6k, long: >6k) and provide p50/p95/p99 latency curves under your concurrency numbers and streaming enabled.
- If you prefer, book a technical deep-dive with Karthik and Ava — they can go deeper into batching, KV cache, and fallback strategies for long contexts.

If I don’t hear back on the token-response split I’ll assume assistant output is ~200 tokens median, 800 tokens p95, 1,500 tokens max for planning purposes.

Thanks — Diego
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 10:12:33 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, streaming & concurrency

Folks — FYI, above thread with AcuityHealth. Key asks for solutions engineering:
- Produce latency profiles (p50/p95/p99) for three context profiles: short (<=1k tokens in), mid (1k–6k in), long (up to 32k in) assuming streaming enabled for interactive. Use Sara’s concurrency: p95 interactive ~120 concurrent, burst 300+ (batched).
- For the long context profile, include two operational options: 1) chunk+stitch recommendation (with cost/latency tradeoffs) and 2) Dedicated instance suggestion (expected p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens).
- Time-to-first-token target: aim for <=150ms for interactive median; include notes on how streaming impacts p95.

Accompanying materials: acuity_slo_req.xlsx (they said they will populate) and latency_samples_stage.csv attached to their reply.

Can you own a short deliverable by EOD Friday? I’ll join the deep-dive if needed.

Thanks — Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
